# Releasing

All eight crates share one version and one `vX.Y.Z` tag. Use [Conventional Commits](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please): `fix:` bumps the patch version, `feat:` bumps the minor version, and `feat!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer marks incompatible changes. Before 1.0, breaking changes also bump the minor version. Keep the same convention in squash-merge titles and preserve breaking-change footers.

After changes reach `main`, release-please opens or updates one release PR. It generates `CHANGELOG.md` and GitHub release notes from the Conventional Commits, including breaking-change descriptions. Write useful commit messages instead of maintaining an `Unreleased` section by hand. Review the generated version, lockfile, changelog, and checks before merging.

Merging the release PR creates the GitHub release and dispatches the existing binary-build and crates.io workflows on the new tag. Ordinary feature PRs do not publish packages. The existing `release` environment and crates.io trusted publisher configuration still apply. Manual runs of the build and publish workflows remain checks only by default; to retry publishing, select the release tag and enable the `publish` input.

All six binary archives include Cohere and Audar: Linux x86_64 CPU, CUDA 12 and CUDA 13, Linux arm64 CPU, and macOS arm64 and x86_64 with Metal. The workflow uses `--features cohere,audar` for CPU/Metal and `--features cuda,audar` for CUDA, installs libclang on Linux, and points macOS bindgen at Xcode's libclang and SDK, including when cross-compiling x86_64. Archives include the native runtime notices and Audar code licenses; model weights are downloaded separately. To check all archives before release, run `gh workflow run release.yml --ref <branch> -f publish=false` and inspect the six build artifacts.

The workflow uses the repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN`; no additional personal token is needed. GitHub's **Settings → Actions → General → Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests** setting must be enabled. If GitHub requests approval for checks on a bot-created release PR, approve those workflow runs before merging.

The root `Cargo.toml` defines `tafrigh-cli` and lists the seven library members explicitly. Each package and internal path dependency declares its version directly. release-please's `rust` strategy updates all eight package versions, their internal dependency requirements, and `Cargo.lock` together in the release PR. `.release-please-manifest.json` records the release baseline. CI checks that all package versions match. Publish in dependency order: `tafrigh`, `tafrigh-transcribe`, `tafrigh-llama`, `tafrigh-wit`, `tafrigh-youtube`, `tafrigh-cohere`, `tafrigh-audar`, then `tafrigh-cli`.

Use each workspace package's actual name as its dependency key, even when its Rust library has a different name. release-please updates path-dependency versions by that key and does not follow Cargo's `package` aliases. CI checks both the keys and version requirements against the workspace packages.

The first publication of a new crate, such as `tafrigh-transcribe`, `tafrigh-llama` or `tafrigh-audar`, requires a crates.io API token in `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` because trusted publishing can only be configured after the crate exists. Configure the new crate's trusted publisher for this repository's `publish.yml` workflow and `release` environment after that first publication.

The workflow explicitly dispatches publishing because a release created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not trigger release-event workflows. See [GitHub's workflow trigger rules](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow) and [release-please's Rust strategy](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/src/strategies/rust.ts).
